absent: Locking, concurrency and interrupt rules for instruction helpers and confidential guest handlers.
Complete structure layouts and allocation lifetimes for decoded instruction, register snapshot, descriptor, emulation context and hypervisor channel.

Semantics of helpers only called but not defined here such as segment selector fetch, descriptor fetch, segment base and bound resolution, mode tests, prefix opcode ModRM SIB fetchers, register offset resolvers and hypervisor call wrappers.
Numeric values of segment identifiers, fault vectors, exit codes, reset values and status flags referenced symbolically.
Selection rule between the two 64 bit address reference variants.
Validation of hypervisor channel setup and shared buffer bounds beyond validity flag checks.

findings.text: Public predicate that reports whether a decoded instruction carries a repeat prefix, used by string move emulation to decide counter update and retry.

Public decoder that classifies a decoded instruction as a memory mapped IO operation and reports the transfer width, distinguishing plain moves, immediate stores, plain loads, zero extending loads, sign extending loads and string moves.

Public accessors that translate the register selector of the ModRM byte into an offset inside the register snapshot and into a direct pointer to that slot, returning a failure indicator when the selector is invalid.
Header utilities shared across units for reading a register slot by offset, combining split descriptor limit fields, and extracting the scale selector from a SIB byte.

Register snapshot is addressed by byte offset with distinct slots for general purpose registers, stack pointer, instruction pointer, flags and segment selectors, allowing generic helpers to locate operands without naming each field.
Segment descriptor exposes its bound as two split portions plus a granularity flag; consumers combine the portions and expand by page size when granularity is set.
Decoded instruction carrier records address width and operand width, decoded prefixes, opcode length and bytes, presence of ModRM and SIB, displacement and immediate payloads and total length.

Confidential guest emulation context pairs a register snapshot with a decoded instruction and a pending fault record; the hypervisor channel provides a shared bounce buffer and saved general registers for parameter passing.
String operation recognition requires a single byte opcode whose value falls in one of three small groups covering input output string moves, block moves and compares, and store load scan families.

Default segment choice is bypassed in 64 bit mode, otherwise it maps address base registers to data, stack or code segments, treats displacement only addressing as data, rejects narrow address width for certain accumulators, and makes destination index string sensitive between extra and data segments.

Segment bound lookup returns zero for a negative selector fetch or null selector or unreadable descriptor, returns all ones in 64 bit or virtual 8086 modes, otherwise combines descriptor limit parts and expands by page granularity with low bits set.
Register slot fetch guards against offsets beyond a maximum by returning zero, and on 32 bit builds narrows segment selector slots to their low half before widening.

Sixteen bit addressing maps the ModRM register-memory selector to fixed pairs drawn from base, base pointer, source index and destination index, passes through direct register operands, and marks displacement only encoding with an invalid sentinel for both slots.

Sixteen bit effective address evaluation requires narrow address width and a present ModRM with memory mode, tolerates invalid component offsets by treating them as zero, adds surviving components with displacement, and reports the first component for segment choice.
Direct register effective address evaluation requires register mode and masks the fetched register value to the active address width before reporting it.

Thirty two and sixty four bit ModRM effective address evaluation rejects register mode, resolves the base selector, substitutes instruction pointer plus length for absent base in 64 bit mode and zero otherwise, then adds displacement with wrapping appropriate to the width.

Scaled indexed addressing requires 32 or 64 bit width with present ModRM and SIB in memory mode, treats absent base or index as zero while rejecting other decode errors, and combines base plus scaled index plus displacement with width appropriate wrapping.

Thirty two bit linear reference formation dispatches among direct register, scaled indexed and plain ModRM paths, resolves segment base and bound, enforces bound outside 64 bit mode, confines virtual 8086 effective values to 16 bits and linear results within a 20 bit range, avoids sign extension, and yields all ones on any failure.

One 64 bit linear reference variant always reports failure, while the other requires wide address width, reuses the same three effective address paths, adds segment base without bound enforcement, and yields all ones on any failure.

Memory mapped IO classification distinguishes single byte move families by operand width versus fixed single byte width, and decodes the two byte escape separately for zero extending and sign extending loads with narrower memory widths.

Memory mapped IO emulation rejects user mode and undecodable operations, fetches the ModRM register slot except for immediate stores and string moves, exchanges payloads through a shared buffer, clears the destination slot before narrow widening loads, and fills with replicated sign for sign extending loads.

String move emulation validates data and extra segment bases, moves one element through a small on stack buffer between source index and destination index, advances both indices forward or backward according to direction flag, decrements the count on repeat, and requests re execution while repeats remain.

Debug control register seven writes are rejected under secure debug swap, require a decodable register source, reject nonzero high half, sanitize reserved bits while forcing one architected bit, refuse early nonzero values without per CPU state, forward the value through the hypervisor channel and cache it; reads return cached state or reset value.

Cache flush is forwarded to the hypervisor, performance counter reads pass counter selector and return two halves only when marked valid, monitor and wait are silent successes without exposing addresses, alignment traps are deferred as faults, and hypercalls carry accumulator and privilege level with optional platform hooks and validity checks.

Virtualization exception dispatcher first validates opcode bytes then routes each exit reason to its handler, covering debug register access, alignment trap, timestamp and counter reads, invalid flush, identification, port IO, model specific registers, hypercall, cache flush, monitor and wait, and nested page faults as MMIO, with anything else unsupported.

MMIO handler operates as a dispatch over decoded operation categories with distinct states for plain store, immediate store, plain load, zero extending load, sign extending load and string move, each completing or propagating hypervisor call failure.

Central entry for confidential guest exception handling receives an emulation context, hypervisor channel and numeric exit reason and returns a status indicating success, retry, decode failure, unsupported, exception injection or hypervisor error.
Instruction evaluation helpers for repeat detection, MMIO classification and ModRM register location form the reusable front end consumed by MMIO and string move emulation.

Callers must treat all ones linear addresses, zero segment bounds, null register pointers, negative offsets and small negative error codes as failures rather than usable values, since every address helper uses them to signal invalid encodings or missing state.

MMIO emulation must not run for user privilege and several paths inject a general protection or alignment fault record instead of proceeding when segment bases are invalid or debug values are illegal.
Hypervisor responses for counter reads and hypercalls must be checked for explicit validity marks before consuming returned registers, otherwise stale channel contents could corrupt guest state.
String operations are identified by single byte opcodes in ranges 6C to 6F, A4 to A7 and AA to AF.
Repeat prefixes are byte values F2 and F3.
MMIO moves use single byte opcodes 88 89 C6 C7 8A 8B A4 A5, with two byte escape 0F followed by B6 B7 for zero extension and BE BF for sign extension.

SIB scale selector occupies the top two bits, address truncation uses 16 bit and 32 bit masks, virtual 8086 linear results stay within a 20 bit range, and page granularity expands limits by 4096 with low 12 bits set.
Debug control writes preserve only bits allowed by mask FFFF23FF hexadecimal, force bit 10 to one, and require the upper 32 bits to be zero.
Descriptor bound combines a low 16 bit part with a high part shifted by 16.
